title: Bayesian computing: exact inference, PyMC and Stan
summary: A complete worked route from probability and exact oracles through actual PyMC computation and self-contained Stan compilation, sampling, diagnostics and decisions.
introduction: The course assumes basic Python and probability, with direct links to prerequisite concepts. Units 001-008 use Python Core, 009-016 use the prepared PyMC 5/ArviZ 0.23 InferenceData environment, and 017-024 compile real Stan in stan-cpu. PyMC demos use two serial chains with 120 warmup and 120 retained draws each. Stan pads use two seeded chains with 100 warmup and 100 retained draws, target acceptance 0.9. These small budgets demonstrate mechanisms and diagnostic limitations; they do not certify convergence and can fail the screen taught in bayes-006: at least four chains, rank-normalized R-hat below 1.01, bulk and tail effective sample sizes of at least about 100 per chain, zero divergences and, for PSIS-LOO in bayes-014, Pareto k below the ArviZ cutoff min(1 - 1/log10(S), 0.7) for S posterior draws. Stan pad data are explicit transformed-data constants. The separate [normal-mean project](projects/normal-mean/README.md) teaches real data.json workflows without implying a JSON editor exists in the classroom. The PyMC 5.28.5 and ArviZ 0.23.4 pins are deliberate. PyMC 6 moved to ArviZ 1, which replaces `arviz.InferenceData` with `xarray.DataTree`, reports 89% equal-tailed intervals by default instead of 94% highest-density intervals and changes which variables `sample_posterior_predictive` resamples. Port these programs deliberately and requalify them rather than mixing current documentation with this environment.
